API reference#

Everything Verse does is plain HTTP on one origin: upload a 3D file, poll the compile, get a signed streaming link, own it, share it privately, pin review comments on it, publish tours and posters, watch the platform. The playground, /studio, the embed SDK and the Blender, Unity and Unreal exporters are all clients of these routes — nothing below is internal.

  • Base URL: https://verse.ctruh.com for the hosted service, or your own origin (Run your own server). Examples write https://HOST.
  • New here? The API quickstart is the three-call version of this page. The Postman collection at /verse-api.postman_collection.json has every route below ready to run (generated from the same route table as the JS/TS SDK — scripts/gen-postman.mjs).
  • History: API changelog.

Every request and response shape on this page was executed against a live server before it was written down.

Conventions#

Requests and responses#

JSON in, JSON out, except where a body is raw bytes (GLB, PNG, upload parts) and where noted (204, 302, SSE). All /v1/* responses are Cache-Control: no-store (exception: /v1/pubkey, public, max-age=300). Scene artifacts under /ingest/* are immutable and cacheable (Cache-Control: public, immutable on hashed artifacts, ranges supported).

Error contract#

Every error the application generates carries the header X-Verse-Error: 1 and a JSON body {"error": "<human-readable cause>"}. Every status ≥ 400 from every route — 400, 401, 402, 404, 405, 409, 413, 429, 500, 503, 507 — follows the rule, static-file 404s included:

Code
curl -sS -D - https://HOST/v1/ingest/does-not-exist
# HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
# X-Verse-Error: 1
# {"error":"unknown job"}

The header is the deterministic tell between the app and the network edge. Hosting proxies occasionally answer a request themselves — a bare 400 on a large or aborted body, a 502/504 on a timeout — and those responses do not carry it. Clients should treat:

  • error + X-Verse-Error: 1 → the app spoke. The error string is authoritative and actionable; do not blind-retry a 4xx (401/413/ 429/507 say exactly what to fix or wait for).
  • error without the header → an intermediary spoke; the app never saw or never finished the request. Transient — one retry is appropriate.

Success responses never carry the header. The bundled exporters implement exactly this rule (integrations/blender/verse_publish/net.py).

On the ingest routes the body also carries errorInfo — the structured twin of error (see Friendly errors). error is always a string.

Authentication#

Three credentials, each optional, each for a different job:

CredentialHeaderGrants
API key vk_…X-API-Key: vk_…upload quota in keyed mode (the operator provisioned ingest/.verse-keys.json; absent file = open mode, no key needed). Daily quota per key, default 512 MB; over → 429; unknown key → 401.
Account token (64 hex)Authorization: Bearer <token> — or the httpOnly verse_session cookie that POST /v1/account/login setsownership of what you publish, the account routes, /studio, moderation, ops reads, and the per-token ingest rate bucket. Returned once at POST /v1/account.
Share token (32 hex)?share=<token> on the URL, or X-Verse-Share: <token>read access to one private scene's artifacts and review comments. Minted by the owner, revocable individually.

A request carrying both an API key and account auth is quota-checked by the key and owned by the account.

People signing in through the website use a six-digit code sent by email or WhatsApp (Sign in); that creates the same verse_session cookie. The code routes (/v1/auth/*) exist for the website only and are not a stable API: scripts and plug-ins keep using the account token.

Plan allowances: 402 and the Verse-Upgrade header#

Every plan has monthly allowances (storage, bandwidth, API calls, Verse Homes, films, room captures, renders, seats, max upload — see Plans and pricing). The server enforces all of them. API calls are requests authenticated with an Authorization: Bearer header (an org API key or an account token); they are counted per account and per key for the billing month. /v1/plans, sign-in and webhooks are never counted, and a browser session (cookie) is not an API call.

At an allowance the route answers 402 Payment Required:

Code
{
  "error": "Your API allowance of 5000 calls this month is used up. Starter includes 50000 API calls a month.",
  "code": "upgrade_required",
  "feature": "apiCallsPerMonth",
  "limit": 5000,
  "used": 5000,
  "plan": "free",
  "suggest": "starter",
  "upgrade_url": "https://verse.ctruh.com/pricing?from=api_call&suggest=starter",
  "nudge": { "type": "limit_100", "title": "…", "body": "…", "url": "https://verse.ctruh.com/n/…", "next": { "plan": "starter", "price": { "amount": 29, "currency": "USD" } } }
}

error, limit, used, plan and upgrade_url are always present (upgradeUrl, relative, is kept for older clients); feature names the allowance (storageGB, bandwidthGB, apiCallsPerMonth, plan2homePerMonth, filmsPerMonth, capturesPerMonth, rendersPerMonth, seats, rawUploadMB, …). The upgrade_url carries the trial offer while the account's trial runs (&offer=trial). A 402 is not retryable until the plan changes or the billing month resets.

Near an allowance (80 % or more of API calls used) every API response carries a Verse-Upgrade header:

Code
Verse-Upgrade: https://verse.ctruh.com/pricing?suggest=starter&from=nudge_limit_80; meter=apiCallsPerMonth; used=82%; plan=free; next=starter

Viewers are never refused: a published scene keeps opening when its owner is over the month's bandwidth (it is served at a lighter quality).

Ingest#

POST /v1/ingest#

Upload a 3D file; the compile runs in the background.

  • Body: the raw bytes — no multipart. A GLB (Content-Type: model/gltf-binary), a Gaussian-splat capture (.splat antimatter15 or INRIA 3DGS binary .ply), a point cloud (.ply with x y z vertices, .las/.laz LAS 1.2–1.4 point formats 0–10, .e57), an IFC building model (.ifc, IFC2x3 / IFC4), a USD scene (.usdz, .usd, .usda, .usdc — one self-contained file; see IFC and USD), or an FBX / OBJ model, alone or in a .zip with its textures (see FBX and OBJ). Max 512 MB one-shot; larger files (up to the plan's raw cap, 2 GB on Free) go through the resumable upload and are prepared on arrival.
  • Headers (optional): X-Verse-Name — slug prefix for the scene id ([a-z0-9-_]); X-Verse-Kind: splat | cloud | ifc | usd | fbx | obj | ply (a PLY mesh) — force the kind (otherwise sniffed: ply\n magic → splat when the 3DGS fields are present, else cloud; LASF / ASTM-E57 magic → cloud; ISO-10303-21 → ifc; #usda, PXR-USDC or a .usdz zip → usd; Kaydara FBX Binary or an ASCII ; FBX header → fbx; OBJ text → obj; a zip holding an .fbx / .obj → fbx / obj — for IFC/USD/FBX/OBJ the bytes decide and the header is only a hint; a 32-byte-aligned body with neither the VPK1 nor glTF magic → splat); X-Verse-Units: m | cm | mm | in | ft — the file's unit for an OBJ (see FBX and OBJ) and, 4.0, for a scan capture that does not declare one (OBJ, PLY, text clouds, E57, LAS; otherwise read from the capture's height); X-Verse-Up: auto | x | y | z | -x | -y | -z — which file axis is up for a capture (otherwise from the surfaces, then the format's convention; GLB and USD keep the frame they declare); X-Verse-Scan: clean | off — force or skip the scan cleanup (levelled floor, debris removed, small holes filled, baked-in light evened out) instead of letting detection decide; the record's scan says what was done — guide: Import a scan; X-Verse-Source — tool attribution; X-API-Key in keyed mode; Authorization: Bearer to own the scene; X-Verse-Bake: preview | final — bake the lighting of a live-lit GLB on the server before compiling (2.7); X-Verse-As: product | interior | building | exterior — say what the file is (the upload card's "3D model or scene?" answer: a model is a product, a scene is walkable); without it the classifier decides; X-Verse-Path: fidelity | streamed — (2.8) take the Fidelity road: the Draco-decoded file itself is published as ingest/<id>.fidelity.glb (textures at source resolution, no compile, seconds), opened by /view?glb=; without the header an upload streams as before and the record's classification says what the shared classifier would pick; X-Verse-Look: studio:neutral|warm|dark[,bg:rrggbb] — the studio preset and backdrop the share link opens with (?look=).
  • Draco-compressed, KHR-quantized and WebP/KTX2-textured GLBs are accepted and normalized server-side.
Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/ingest \
  -H "Content-Type: model/gltf-binary" -H "X-Verse-Name: docs-demo" \
  --data-binary @scene.glb
# HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
# {"job":"docs-demo-718035483f84"}
  • Validation: right after the upload, before a compile is queued, the server inspects the file (magic bytes; for a GLB its JSON chunk — meshes, triangles, external references, required extensions). A file it cannot build still answers 202 {job}; the job's first poll is then status: "error" with a friendly error. Nothing was compiled and any key quota is refunded.
  • Response 202: { "job": "<id>" }. The job id is the scene id. - Errors: 400 malformed · 401 unknown/missing key (keyed mode) · 413 over 512 MB · 429 rate limit or quota (body says which) · 503 compile queue full · 507 storage full — refused before the body is read when free space is below max(VERSE_MIN_FREE_MB, 3× the declared size).

GET /v1/ingest/<job>#

Fidelity mode (2.8) adds to a done record: path ("fidelity" | "streamed"), glbUrl (https://HOST/ingest/<id>.fidelity.glb), classification ({ kind, path, plan, evidence, requested, resolved, reason? } — the verdict with its evidence: meshes, triangles, textures, maxTextureDim, decodedMB, longestSide, lights, lighting), look, digest (sha256:<hex> of the artifact) and signature (base64 Ed25519 over that digest under the server's signing key, the .vpk trailer's twin), stats.mode: "fidelity"; arUrl as for a streamed scene.

Poll every few seconds until status leaves "compiling". Small models compile in seconds; multi-million-triangle scans in minutes. estimateS is the expected build time, calibrated against this server's recent builds of similar size (falling back to ~8 s per source MB, floor 15 s).

A finished record may carry prepare: { inputBytes, outputBytes, resized, meshesInstanced, seconds } when the server ran verse-prepare on the upload (it does not when the file arrived with the marker), and its fixes line says what changed.

Compile stages#

While compiling, stage is live text. In pipeline order:

stageMeaning
preparingupload accepted; payload being normalized (Draco rewrite, KTX2 transcode)
converting(2.7) an IFC / USD upload is being converted to glTF (web-ifc / tinyusdz); the record's convert { kind, phase, done, total } and workText follow the product count, progress runs 0.02–0.10
baking(2.7) the cloud bake is tracing the lighting into lightmaps (X-Verse-Bake); the record's bake { quality, phase, done, total } and workText follow its progress, progress runs 0.03–0.15
queuedwaiting for a compile slot (two concurrent compiles per origin)
remoteclaimed by an external fleet worker; its own stage reports follow
texturestexture encode / atlas phase (also the stage of every retry — attempt and healing say which)
geometrymeshlet-DAG build (clusters, LOD hierarchy)
packingwriting the container (.vpk; the whole pack phase for .vsp splat and .vpc point-cloud jobs)
signingEd25519-signing the finished file
verifyingchecking the built scene before it goes live (integrity, signature, counts, bounds, texture streams, staging)
uploadingstoring the artifact in the bucket (VERSE_STORAGE=s3 only)
publishingpublishing the model in compatibility mode (the lossless fallback)

Treat the value as informational — fleet workers may report additional lowercase [a-z-] stages; never gate behaviour on a specific string.

Friendly errors#

No raw compiler, OS or runtime text ever reaches an uploader. Every failure the ingest path can produce maps to one entry of a single taxonomy (web/playground/upload-care.js, shared by the server and the app):

  • error — always a string: one friendly sentence plus its fix. Safe to print verbatim; exporters and the embed SDK need no change.
  • errorInfo — { code, title, message, fix, retryable }. retryable answers "is trying the same file again worthwhile?".

Self-healing#

A compile that fails for a recoverable reason is retried automatically — deterministically, up to 3 attempts, inside the 45-minute wall clock:

FailureNext attempt
interrupted (SIGTERM on a restart, a spawn that could not start)re-run as it was
out of memory (killed), per-attempt timeout, or stalled (no output and no CPU for 10 min — VERSE_COMPILE_STALL_S)lighter texture settings: fewer streamed materials, a smaller byte budget, no 4096² hero tier; fewer encode threads after a memory kill, a shorter texture deadline after a timeout
the output failed verification (a fleet worker's result included)rebuilt on the next rung
still failinglast compile rung: the low-memory ETC1S texture path (VERSE_TEX_SAFE), one encode thread, a small streamed set. Geometry and the preview atlas are untouched
every rung failed, or the wall clock ran outthe lossless fallback: the job still ends done

Bad input and server faults (disk full, a compiler crash) are not retried — a server fault goes straight to the lossless fallback. The encode cache stays in effect across attempts, so a retry reuses every texture the failed attempt already encoded. While a retry runs the record carries attempt and healing; a healed scene reports stats.healed: true and attempts. Splat packs are not retried.

Verify before done#

A compiled scene is checked before its job is marked done (stage verifying), so a bad output is never handed out as a link:

CheckFails when
opensthe file is not a readable .vpk
integritythe contents do not match the hash the compiler recorded (truncated, altered)
signaturethe Ed25519 signature is missing or does not verify — repaired by signing again
countsno clusters or triangles; the full-detail level does not carry the source's triangles; a payload range lies outside the file
boundsbounds are not finite, reach outside the source's bounds (2 % tolerance), or collapsed to a fraction of them
texture-streamsa referenced texture stream, the preview atlas or the collision grid is missing from the file
stagingthe .stage.json spawn is not finite, is implausibly far away, or — for an object-scale scene (largest extent under 2 m) — sits inside the object. Repaired by removing the spawn from the manifest (the tour and the floor plan stay): the viewer then frames the scene itself

A finding with a repair is fixed on the spot and re-checked (verify.repaired). Anything else fails the attempt: the scene is rebuilt on the next rung of the ladder and, past that, published through the lossless fallback. The hook is pluggable — OUTPUT_CHECKS in web/playground/verify-output.mjs.

Lossless fallback#

When every rung fails, the output keeps failing verification, or the 45-minute wall clock runs out, the uploader still gets a working link: the prepared model itself is published through the viewer's non-virtualized classic path.

Code
{ "status": "done",
  "url": "https://HOST/?model=ingest/villa-0413581a2dd3.classic.glb",
  "modelUrl": "https://HOST/ingest/villa-0413581a2dd3.classic.glb",
  "stats": { "mode": "classic", "tris": 184220 },
  "fallback": { "mode": "classic", "reason": "out_of_memory" },
  "notice": "Published in compatibility mode: full quality, larger download.",
  "attempts": 3 }
  • url is a share link like any other; there is no vpkUrl. Embed it with data-model="<modelUrl>" rather than data-scene.
  • The file is the uploaded model after normalization (Draco decoded) — the link therefore serves the source geometry and textures in full.
  • Offered for prepared models up to VERSE_CLASSIC_FALLBACK_MB (default 96; 0 disables it; published as limits.classicFallbackMaxMB). Larger models, splat captures and unreadable files fail with the friendly taxonomy instead.
  • The operator is alerted on Slack and the ops history records the outcome classic-fallback.
  • Animated and rigged models take this path by design. A streamed scene is static, so a model with animations or skins that fits the size cap is published here directly — no compile attempt — with fallback.reason: "animated", a notice saying the animation was kept, and the ops outcome classic-animated (no Slack alert). A larger animated model compiles as a static streamed scene.

POST /v1/ingest/<job>/contact#

Attach the uploader's contact to a job — the app's "email me when it's live" form. JSON body, max 4 KB:

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/ingest/docs-demo-718035483f84/contact \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"Asha Rao","phone":"+91 98765 43210","email":"asha@example.com","consent":true}'
# {"ok":true,"emailConfigured":true,"emailed":false,"notify":"when-live"}
  • name (2–80 chars), email, phone (7–15 digits; +, 00, spaces, dashes and brackets accepted) and consent: true are all required.
  • notify: "when-live" — an email goes out when the job reaches done (or an apology if it finally fails); "sent" — the job had already finished, the email went immediately; "follow-up" — this server has no mail provider configured, nothing is sent and the operator follows up.
  • One scene mails one address: a different address after the email went out is 409.
  • Errors: 400 { error, field } on invalid input · 404 unknown or expired job · 429 (12 per hour per IP).
  • The contact is stored on the server in a private file, is never served, never appears in a job record and is never logged in full.

Auto-staging sidecars#

Scenes whose compile produced a walk-collision grid also emit, beside the artifact:

  • <id>.stage.json — { "spawn": { "position", "yaw" }, "tour": { "samples": [[t,x,y,z,fx,fy,fz], …] }, "bounds": { "min", "max" }, "kind": "interior" | "object" | "open", "walk": true | false, "view": { "mode": "walk" | "orbit", "eye", "look", "radius" } }. kind is what the scene is: an interior (ceilinged, person-sized free space) opens at view — standing at the spawn in walk mode; an object (nowhere a person could stand) has no spawn, walk: false, an orbit view framing the whole object from outside and a turntable tour, and no .plan.svg; an open scene (walkable ground under open sky) has no view and opens on the overview orbit. Manifests written before kind existed carry only the first three fields and behave as before. ?view=overview on the viewer skips the opening view. The spawn is a walkable interior pick (on the main walkable floor, clear of walls and furniture); the tour is a loop in the /v1/tour sample format — for interiors a 20–60 s walkthrough **planned through free space** on the collision grid (room targets, A* with wall clearance, smoothed and re-validated, ~0.9 m/s, yaw ≤ 45°/s; rows every 0.2 s), an orbit for open-sky scenes, a slow pan at the spawn when an interior has no routable rooms. Scenes compiled before 2026-10-01 carry the old straight-leg tour and must be re-ingested to get a planned one. The viewer applies the spawn and offers Tour and Export video when a plain ?vpk= link loads (no tour → no chip).
  • <id>.plan.svg — a deterministic 2D floor plan (walkable floor, walls, spawn dot, scale bar, north arrow, area label); data-nx/nz/ cell/ox/oz carry the grid mapping. The minimap uses it as its base.
  • <id>.usdz — (2.7) the iOS AR Quick Look package of a product-scale scene (GET /ingest/<id>.usdz, model/vnd.usdz+zip, immutable, the scene's visibility and ?v= version key), built from the prepared GLB at compile time; the record's arUrl points at it and ar carries the report or the reason there is none. Put it in <a rel="ar"><img></a> and Safari opens it in AR — guides/view-in-ar.md.

Retention#

Account-owned scenes are permanent. Unowned scenes are retained best-effort: when compiled scenes exceed the disk budget (VERSE_VPK_BUDGET_MB, default 3500), the least-recently-opened unowned .vpk/.vsp and its sidecars are evicted. Uploaded source files are deleted after compile — except for a scene published through the lossless fallback, where the uploaded GLB is the scene. Finished job records expire after 2 h; compile intermediates are swept after 2 h.

Bake for me (2.7)#

A live-lit GLB — lights in the file (KHR_lights_punctual), no lightmaps — streams with the engine's live lighting. Ask for a cloud bake and the server traces the lighting into lightmaps before it compiles, so the link streams with the baked look (the path the renderer does best; see the guide):

  • POST /v1/ingest with X-Verse-Bake: preview (or final); resumable uploads pass "bake": "preview" | "final" in the begin body (the header on commit also works). 1/true mean preview. Ignored for splats and point clouds.
  • preview: lightmaps up to 1024² per material, a 24 M-texel scene budget, 64 samples per texel, one indirect bounce, ≤ ~10 min on a 3 M-triangle flat. final: 2048², 96 M texels, 256 samples, two bounces, ≤ ~30 min.
  • Surfaces no visitor can see from the walkable floor (the compiler's occupancy grid) are not traced and get a flat ambient level; the report's hiddenAreaFraction says how much that was.
  • The job passes through stage: "baking" with live counters (bake.phase visibility | lightmaps | texels, done, total, plus workText). The done record carries bake (the report, above) and a fixes line ("Baked the lighting for you (preview quality): …"). The published link is the baked scene; stats.mode and verification are as for any upload.
  • A scene the bake cannot carry — animated or skinned, already baked, nothing bakeable (all glass / unlit / cut-out) — or a bake that fails or runs past its cap (VERSE_BAKE_TIMEOUT_S, default 15 min preview / 45 min final) is compiled live-lit as it came; the record says so in bake.skipped and fixes. VERSE_BAKE=0 turns the stage off.
  • The upload screen offers the same thing as its Lighting choice (2.7.2): Keep as exported (the default — no bake), Bake for me · preview or Bake for me · final, shown on every live-lit upload. Preflight records carry lighting: "live" | "baked" | "unlit" and lights.
Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/ingest -H "Content-Type: model/gltf-binary" \
  -H "X-Verse-Name: flat-a" -H "X-Verse-Bake: preview" --data-binary @flat-a.glb
# … poll: {"status":"compiling","stage":"baking","bake":{"quality":"preview","phase":"lightmaps","done":12,"total":40},"workText":"Baking lighting · lightmap 12 of 40"}
# … done: {"status":"done","bake":{"quality":"preview","seconds":312.4,"texels":18200000,"lightmaps":40,"hiddenAreaFraction":0.31,…},"fixes":["Baked the lighting for you (preview quality): …"]}

Resumable uploads#

For clients whose single large POST keeps dying mid-body (edge proxies are unkind to 100 MB+ requests). Same pipeline, different transport: commit answers the exact 202 {job} the one-shot path does and everything from GET /v1/ingest/<job> on is identical. The Blender add-on switches to this flow automatically above 100 MB.

POST /v1/ingest/begin#

  • Body: { "size": <bytes>, "name"?: "<slug>", "kind"?: "splat", "prepared"?: true, "bake"?: "preview" | "final", "path"?, "look"?, "scan"?, "up"?, "units"? } (the last five are the body spellings of X-Verse-Path / -Look / -Scan / -Up / -Units; the headers also work on commit) — size is the exact total length: 1 … the plan's raw cap (Free 500 MB, Starter 2 GB, Pro 10 GB, Scale 20 GB, Enterprise custom — rawUploadMB in plans.json; past it, or past the plan's storage with the files you already have, 402 upgrade_required, past the server's own VERSE_MAX_RAW_MB 400 file_too_large). Send anything over 64 MB through this resumable path; the one-shot POST /v1/ingest keeps its 512 MB door. The server prepares every model on arrival (convert, right-size textures, merge duplicates, instance repeated meshes) and the plan's size limit (Free 500 MB, Starter 2 GB, Pro 10 GB, Scale 20 GB) applies to the prepared size: over it, stronger tiers run automatically (2K, then 1K textures; colour maps to JPEG, normal maps stay lossless), then the job pauses with prepare.state: "choice" and the 402 upgrade shape (prepare.choice.deny) — answer with POST /v1/ingest/<job>/choice {"action":"compress"|"cancel"|"recheck"}; upgrading the plan lets the same job carry on by itself. "prepared": true (verse-prepare ran on your side) still reads the plan's prepared limit. The job record carries prepare (state, line such as "943 MB → 292 MB · 405 textures optimised · 41 meshes reused", tiers) and, for an FBX / OBJ naming textures that were not in the upload, convert.textureWarning (count, names, message) — non-blocking.
  • Rate, quota and storage gates run here (this is the upload's debit).
Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/ingest/begin -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"size":1696,"name":"docs-resumable"}'
# {"uploadId":"c5de5f9fdbf9aab0","received":0,"size":1696}
  • Errors: 400 bad size · 401/429 key/quota/rate · 503 too many open uploads · 507 storage full.

PUT /v1/ingest/part/<uploadId>#

Append one part. Strictly ordered, one at a time: the part's Content-Range start must equal the server's current received.

Code
curl -sS -X PUT https://HOST/v1/ingest/part/c5de5f9fdbf9aab0 \
  -H "Content-Range: bytes 0-847/1696" --data-binary @part1.bin
# {"uploadId":"c5de5f9fdbf9aab0","received":848,"size":1696}
  • Errors: 400 malformed or mismatched range / body length (a torn body rolls back to the last good offset) · 404 unknown or expired upload · 409 out of order — the body carries the authoritative offset; resume from there:
Code
{ "error": "out-of-order part: next byte is 848", "received": 848 }

A 409 whose received equals the part's own start means **another attempt at this part is still in flight** ("another part is already uploading"): wait and retry. A writer that has sent nothing for 30 s (VERSE_PART_STALL_S) is cut when the next attempt arrives, so a client that vanished behind a proxy never holds the upload for long.

  • Refusals are readable. A refused part of up to 64 MB is answered and its body drained rather than the connection cut, so clients that stream the body without Expect: 100-continue (Node's fetch) read the status instead of a reset ("fetch failed").

GET /v1/ingest/part/<uploadId>#

200 { uploadId, received, size } — how a client that lost its connection learns where to resume. After a server restart received is the number of bytes that actually reached the disk (it may sit in the middle of the part that was in flight). A committed upload also carries job.

POST /v1/ingest/commit/<uploadId>#

Send the same auth headers as a one-shot upload (X-API-Key debits the quota here; Authorization: Bearer stamps the owner).

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/ingest/commit/c5de5f9fdbf9aab0
# HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
# {"job":"docs-resumable-c47d410e4f51"}
  • Errors: 401/429 · 404 unknown/expired upload · 409 upload incomplete (body carries received/size) · 503 compile queue full.
  • Idempotent: committing an already-committed upload answers the same 202 {job} — retry a commit whose response was lost.

Upload sessions survive server restarts. Each open upload is recorded on the server (ingest/.uploads/, never served); after a restart GET /v1/ingest/part/<uploadId> answers the true received and the client continues from there. A client should treat a network error or a gateway status (502/503/504 without X-Verse-Error) on any of these routes as "the server is away": wait, GET the part to resync, carry on. The web app does exactly that (web/playground/upload-transport.js) and shows "Reconnecting — your upload is safe" meanwhile. 2 hours of inactivity (VERSE_UPLOAD_STALE_MS) expires a session and later requests answer 404. A 404/405 on begin is also how an older server without these routes announces itself — fall back to one-shot.

Upload from URL#

POST /v1/ingest/url — the server fetches the file itself and compiles it exactly like a body upload. For automation platforms (Zapier, Make, n8n) and CMS media libraries, where the file already has a URL and should not pass through the automation platform.

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/ingest/url -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"url":"https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/…/palm-villa.glb?dl=1","name":"palm-villa"}'
# HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
# {"job":"palm-villa-3f1c9a2b7e04","sizeBytes":48213990,"source":"uc1234.dl.dropboxusercontent.com"}
  • Body (JSON, ≤ 4 KB): url (required, absolute http(s)), name (scene name; default: the file name in the URL), kind (as X-Verse-Kind; default: from the URL's extension, the bytes decide), bake, path, look, scan (as the resumable begin). X-Verse-Kind / X-Api-Key / Authorization headers work as on POST /v1/ingest.
  • What is fetched. Public addresses only: the host name is resolved by the server and every address must be routable (no loopback, private, link-local / cloud-metadata, CGNAT, multicast; IPv6 ULA / link-local / v4-mapped alike), the request goes to the vetted address (the name travels as Host / SNI, so a DNS answer cannot change between check and use), redirects are followed by hand (at most 3, each re-vetted), the download is streamed to disk and cut at the upload limit (512 MB; a Content-Length over it is refused before a byte is read), 10 minutes wall clock. A Dropbox share link needs dl=1; a Google Drive link needs "Anyone with the link"; S3 / R2 / GCS work with a presigned URL.
  • Answer: the one-shot 202 {job} plus sizeBytes and source (the host the file came from). Poll GET /v1/ingest/<job> as usual.
  • Errors (same contract, errorInfo.code): 400 url_blocked (not http(s), credentials in the URL, a private / local / unresolvable host), 400 bad_request (no url), 400 empty_file, 404 url_fetch_failed (the URL answered 404), 413 file_too_large, 502/504 url_fetch_failed (the URL did not give a file, ended early, redirected too often, timed out), 401 / 429 / 503 / 507 as POST /v1/ingest. Rate-limited with the ingest bucket.

Splat captures#

POST /v1/ingest with a .splat/.ply body (and ideally X-Verse-Kind: splat) packs a streamed .vsp instead of compiling a mesh. Same limits, quotas, rate buckets and polling (stage packing):

Code
{
  "status": "done",
  "url":    "https://HOST/?model=ingest/room-9f3a01b2c4d5.vsp",
  "vspUrl": "https://HOST/ingest/room-9f3a01b2c4d5.vsp",
  "stats":  { "splats": 1200000, "chunks": 160 },
  "signed": true
}

.vsp files are Ed25519-signed like .vpk scans (an 80-byte trailer over the head the browser already fetched). Splat jobs always pack on the origin — the compile fleet runs verse-compile only. WebGPU tiers only in the viewer.

Point clouds#

POST /v1/ingest with a .ply (xyz vertices, no 3DGS fields), .las, .laz, .e57 or .xyz / .pts text body — X-Verse-Kind: cloud recommended; LAS/LAZ (LASF) and E57 (ASTM-E57) are sniffed by magic, a plain .ply by its header — packs a streamed .vpc octree (docs/vpc-format.md) instead of compiling a mesh. Same limits, quotas, rate buckets and polling (stage packing); input cap 200 M points (limits.maxCloudPoints; cloud_too_many otherwise, cloud_invalid for unreadable files):

Code
{
  "status": "done",
  "url":    "https://HOST/?model=ingest/scan-9f3a01b2c4d5.vpc",
  "vpcUrl": "https://HOST/ingest/scan-9f3a01b2c4d5.vpc",
  "stats":  { "points": 5000000, "nodes": 509 },
  "signed": true
}

.vpc files are Ed25519-signed with the .vsp trailer convention (VPCS). Cloud jobs always pack on the origin. The viewer streams them in both tiers (WebGPU and WebGL2); ?cloud=scale,min,max,lit tunes the point discs. Text clouds: one point per line, x y z with optional intensity, colour (0–255 or 0–1) and normal. Formats not read: ASCII LAS text dumps, PTX, .e57 spherical-only scans without Cartesian data.

IFC and USD (2.7)#

POST /v1/ingest with an .ifc (IFC2x3 or IFC4 STEP) or a single-file USD (.usdz, .usd, .usda, .usdc) body — X-Verse-Kind: ifc | usd is a hint; the bytes decide (ISO-10303-21, #usda, PXR-USDC, a zip whose first entry is a .usd* layer). The upload is **converted on the server** (stage converting; tools/ifc-convert: web-ifc for IFC, tinyusdz for USD — both WASM) into a glTF where **every product / Mesh prim is one node** carrying its identity in extras, then takes the ordinary mesh road (prepare → compile → sign → verify). The compiler builds one detail hierarchy per product, so every streamed cluster belongs to exactly one object at every level of detail — a click names the object, and hiding a storey removes its pixels, in both tiers.

Code
{
  "status": "done",
  "url":      "https://HOST/?vpk=ingest/house-9f3a01b2c4d5.vpk",
  "vpkUrl":   "https://HOST/ingest/house-9f3a01b2c4d5.vpk",
  "propsUrl": "https://HOST/ingest/house-9f3a01b2c4d5.props.json",
  "stats":    { "mode": "streamed", "tris": 48, "clusters": 4, "products": 4 },
  "convert":  { "kind": "ifc", "schema": "IFC4", "products": 4, "triangles": 48, "materials": 3, "storeys": 2, "skipped": 0, "seconds": 0.1 },
  "fixes":    ["Converted the IFC model (IFC4) on our side: 4 objects, 48 triangles, 2 storeys in 1 s. Click any object in the link for its properties."]
}
  • <id>.props.json — the object index, served next to the scene under the same rules as .stage.json; the scene's .stage.json carries "props": true so viewers fetch the sidecar only when it exists (private scenes: owner or share token only; versioned, deleted and backed up with the scene): { "version": 1, "source": "ifc" | "usd", "schema", "products", "nodes": { "<glTF node>": { "id", "type", "name", "storey"?, "description"?, "tag"?, "props": { "Pset_WallCommon.IsExternal": true, … }, "bounds"? } }, "ids": { "<GlobalId | prim path>": node }, "storeys": [ { "name", "elevation"?, "id"?, "nodes": […] } ], "types": { "IfcWall": [nodes…] }, "clusters": { "count", "runs": [[firstCluster, count, node | -1], …] } }. For IFC id is the GlobalId, type the entity (IfcWall), storey the containing IfcBuildingStorey, and props the flattened property sets and quantities (Pset.Property → value; type psets included); for USD id is the prim path, type is Mesh and storey the group below the root prim. bounds is the world AABB.
  • Viewer: the share link grows an Objects panel (tree by storey and type with visibility toggles, search by name / id / type, the selected object's property sets); clicking an object selects it; ?select=<id> deep-links to one. Hidden objects are dropped before the cut test in both tiers (never drawn, never requested).
  • Embed SDK: viewer.getProperties(id) / getProperties(), viewer.setVisible(ids, bool) / isolate(ids) / setVisible("all"), viewer.select(id, { frame }); events objects, select, visibility, and pick carries object. @ctruhtech/verse-sdk: kind: "ifc" | "usd" (and, 3.0, "fbx" | "obj") on upload(); JobRecord.propsUrl / convert.
  • What is read: IFC2x3 and IFC4 body geometry through web-ifc (every product with a representation; IfcSpace, openings, annotations and grids are skipped; unstyled products take a per-type palette); USD Mesh prims (any face size, triangulated), xform chains, the stage's upAxis (Z-up is stood upright) and metersPerUnit; materials from a MaterialX network (OpenPBR ND_open_pbr_surface_surfaceshader; Autodesk ND_standard_surface_surfaceshader in .usda text layers) or UsdPreviewSurface → glTF PBR with clearcoat, sheen, transmission, specular, IOR and emissive-strength extensions; base colour, normal, emissive, occlusion and metallic/roughness textures inside the file (the last two packed into one). convert adds materialX, standardSurface, previewSurface (materials per model), extensions, upAxis, metersPerUnit. Files over 160 MB use tinyusdz's 64-bit build. Not read: IFC files over the 512 MB cap, USD references / payloads / sublayers to files outside the upload (usdz carries its own), skinning, animation, point instancers, Standard Surface inside binary crates (.usdc / .usdz — their UsdPreviewSurface is used), texture connections on Standard Surface. Conversion runs under the compile semaphore with a 15-minute budget (VERSE_CONVERT_TIMEOUT_S); BIM jobs always compile on the origin. Guide: docs/guides/publish-from-ifc.md.

FBX and OBJ (3.0)#

POST /v1/ingest with an .fbx (binary or ASCII, FBX 2011–2020 / 7.1–7.7), an .obj, or a .zip holding either with its .mtl and textures — X-Verse-Kind: fbx | obj is a hint; the bytes decide. The upload is converted on the server (stage converting, phases unpack → transcode (ASCII FBX) → import → export; tools/model-convert: headless Blender 5.0, ASCII FBX transcoded to binary first, MTL texture paths repaired against the zip) into a GLB that then takes the **ordinary GLB road**: verse-prepare, classification from the converted GLB, Fidelity (X-Verse-Path: fidelity for a product) or streamed. No props sidecar.

Code
{
  "status": "done",
  "url": "https://HOST/?vpk=ingest/boat-9f3a01b2c4d5.vpk",
  "convert": { "kind": "fbx", "schema": "FBX 7.4 ASCII", "container": "zip", "products": 115,
               "triangles": 3747008, "materials": 28, "images": 95, "pbrUpgraded": 28,
               "units": "from the FBX header", "size": [36.2, 19.9, 23.8], "animations": 0, "skins": 0,
               "missingTextures": [], "missingTextureCount": 0, "seconds": 72.1 },
  "fixes": ["Converted the FBX 7.4 ASCII file on our side (from the zip): 115 objects, 3,747,008 triangles, 28 materials, 95 textures — 36 × 20 × 24 m; 28 PBR materials (3ds Max Physical / Stingray / Arnold) mapped in 1 min."]
}
  • Units and axes: FBX from the file's UnitScaleFactor and UpAxis (a centimetre Z-up 3ds Max file lands in metres, Y-up). OBJ has no units: X-Verse-Units (m | cm | mm | in | ft; SDK units) says which; without it a model wider than 1,000 units is read as centimetres and wider than 100,000 as millimetres (convert.units says what was assumed).
  • Materials: Phong / Lambert; 3ds Max Physical, Maya Stingray PBS and Arnold base values and maps (convert.pbrUpgraded counts them); MTL Kd / Ke / Pr / Pm and map_*. Embedded FBX textures always; separate files when zipped. Missing ones are listed in convert.missingTextures and the fix line; the upload still builds.
  • Animation: node animation and skins, one clip (convert.animations is 1 when anything moves; static takes are dropped). OBJ: none.
  • Zip rules: Deflate or stored, no password, zip64 fine; entries that escape the folder are skipped; unpacked size capped (VERSE_ZIP_MAX_BYTES, 20 GB); other scene files (.max, .blend, USD, glTF) are not unpacked.
  • Errors: model_invalid (not retryable) — not FBX/OBJ bytes, FBX older than 7.1, a zip without a model, a file Blender cannot read; convert_failed (retryable) — the converter crashed or ran past VERSE_CONVERT_TIMEOUT_S (15 min), or Blender is not installed on the server. Guide: docs/guides/upload-fbx-obj.md.

Accounts & Studio#

Accounts add ownership, analytics, privacy and moderation on top of ingest. There is no e-mail and no password: the account token is the credential, like an API key.

The token is returned once, at creation. It cannot be recovered or rotated (delete-and-recreate is the rotation story). Anyone holding it controls the account.

Accounts sit beside keyed mode: anonymous uploads and every existing share link behave exactly as before. Auth on every account route (and on any ingest, poster, tour or experience publish that should carry an owner): Authorization: Bearer <token>, or the verse_session cookie.

POST /v1/account#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/account -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"Docs Demo"}'
# {"accountId":"acct-5fab29f5aa8e","name":"Docs Demo","createdAt":1790833829999,
#  "token":"<64 hex, shown once>",

Webhooks (2.7)#

Per-account receivers for the things an integration waits on. Events:

EventWhendata
scene.readya job the account owns finished{ job, scene, status: "done", url, vpkUrl?, stats? } (scene = the scene id, the same as job)
scene.failed…or failed (the friendly error, never the raw detail){ job, scene, status: "error", error, code }

A delivery is one POST of { "id", "event", "t", "account", "data" } with Content-Type: application/json and the headers X-Verse-Event, X-Verse-Delivery (the id), X-Verse-Timestamp (unix seconds) and X-Verse-Signature: sha256=<hex> — HMAC-SHA256 with the hook's secret over <timestamp>.<raw body>. Verify by recomputing it over the bytes you received and comparing in constant time; reject stale timestamps. A non-2xx answer, a timeout (10 s) or an unreachable host is retried: 3 tries, backoff 2 s then 8 s. Redirects are not followed and the receiver's response body is never read or stored.

Code
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
const expected = "sha256=" + createHmac("sha256", SECRET).update(`${req.headers["x-verse-timestamp"]}.${rawBody}`).digest("hex");
const ok = timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(expected), Buffer.from(req.headers["x-verse-signature"] ?? ""));

Or, with @ctruhtech/verse-sdk (WebCrypto — Node 18+, Workers, Deno, Bun): await verifyWebhook({ secret, body: rawBody, signature, timestamp }) — constant-time, rejects timestamps more than 5 minutes off. Copy-paste receivers: developers.md § Webhooks.

Visibility & share tokens#

  • unlisted (default) — reachable by anyone with the URL, listed nowhere.
  • public — reserved for a future gallery; serves identically to unlisted today.
  • private — every artifact (.vpk/.vsp, .stage.json, .plan.svg, poster) and the scene's review comments require the owner's auth or a share token. Everyone else gets a 404 byte-identical to a missing file's, plus X-Verse-Private: 1 so the viewer can say "This scene is private". Range requests work unchanged for anyone granted access.
Code
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://HOST/ingest/docs-demo-718035483f84.vpk
# HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
# X-Verse-Private: 1
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -H "Range: bytes=0-1023" \
  "https://HOST/ingest/docs-demo-718035483f84.vpk?share=<shareToken>"
# HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
# Cache-Control: private, no-store

Share tokens are 16 random bytes (32 hex), returned once, stored as SHA-256 hashes, compared in constant time, never logged. Pass ?share= on the share link (the app threads it onto every artifact fetch, including the worker's range requests) or on artifact URLs, or send X-Verse-Share. Deleting the scene or losing ownership revokes them all.

CDN caveat: with VERSE_CDN_BASE set, unlisted/public artifacts > 302 to the edge; a private scene never redirects — CDN copies are public bytes with no auth in front. Flipping an already-cached scene private does not purge the edge; purge it there.

Anonymous (ownerless) scenes have no visibility record and can never be private until an owner claims them. Step-by-step: Share privately with tokens.

Definitions. A view is one browser tab opening the scene (a session); a session belongs to the UTC day of its first row. Unique viewers are distinct browser ids; returning ones opened the scene in two or more sessions in the range. Time is visible time: look samples × 2 s. Interacted = a drag, tap, wheel or key on the page, or walking. Stayed 30 s+ = at least 15 samples. Enquired = a click on the enquiry button. Rooms come from the scene's floor plan (.plan.svg): indoor vs open sky (the plan's data-open layer, or ray casting on older plans), then a watershed over the distance-to-wall field — passages up to 1.25 m wide (doorways) separate rooms, wider openings join them, slivers under 3 m² merge into a neighbour, narrow long rooms are corridors. A room is named by the owner (PUT …/rooms), else after the default experience's hotspot standing in it, else "Room N" / "Corridor N" by area; its key (its centre, to 0.5 m) keeps stored days and names attached across re-segmentation. Samples under open sky read "Outdoors (terrace / garden)", samples off the plan "Overview (outside the floor plan)". A scene without an interior plan reports no rooms (roomsSource: "none"). The heatmap is framed to the plan; samples outside it are listed in heatmap.outside with their edge position (ex, ez).

Viewer report. The page is /studio/report?scene=<id> for the owner and /r/<token> for a shared link. A visit's source is one key: embed when it ran in an iframe; else the in-app browser it opened in (whatsapp, instagram, facebook, linkedin, twitter, tiktok, snapchat, telegram, wechat, line); else the referring site's class (google, search, email, youtube, other…); else share (a private share link) or direct (typed, a QR code, an app that sends no referrer). A viewer is one browser id; their source is how they first arrived, their device the one they used last. A viewer's id in a report (V- + 6 hex) is a further keyed hash of the stored pseudonym, scoped to the scene — it is stable within the scene's reports and is never the stored value. Hotspot opens count every opening of a hotspot (by its id); questions count questions asked in Ask Verse while the scene was open — never their text. The viewer table keeps at most 5000 viewers per scene-day.

Storage. Raw rows live in the telemetry log (rotated at ~32 MB, one rotation kept). An hour after a UTC day ends it is rolled up per scene into ingest/.analytics/<id>/<day>.json (counts and capped maps — no rows, no raw ids) and kept for VERSE_ANALYTICS_KEEP_DAYS days (default 400; days older than that are pruned and never reported). Deleting a scene deletes its roll-ups.

Privacy. Analytics rows posted to /v1/telemetry are rebuilt from a whitelist before they are stored (any other field is dropped); the browser id is stored as a keyed HMAC (per-install salt in ingest/.analytics/.salt); no IP is ever written. Requests with DNT: 1 or Sec-GPC: 1 are answered 204 with X-Verse-Analytics: off and not stored.

A camera path is the owner's authored walkthrough: keyframes recorded in the viewer (Path → Record), stored beside the scene as <id>.paths.json. Each key carries p (eye) and f (forward), and optionally fov (vertical degrees, 5–150), dur (seconds to the next key; absent = auto from distance and turn), hold (dwell seconds), ease (smooth — default — · stop · linear), look (a look-at target: two consecutive keys with one keep it framed) and label (the chapter name, ≤ 80 chars). mode: walk (eye height over the floor, collision-safe) or fly; speed in m/s for auto timing. The viewer bakes it with a centripetal Catmull-Rom spline, squad orientation and arc-length timing (verse_core::campath). POST creates (the first path becomes the default), PUT /paths/<pid> replaces ("default": true also makes it the default), PUT /paths {default: pid|null} picks the share link's default, DELETE removes. Writes are owner-only; GETs mirror the scene's visibility, Cache-Control: no-store. A share link plays a path with ?path=<pid> (or ?path=default). Limits: 24 paths per scene, 2–256 keys, 96 KB per body. Errors: 400 malformed key / bad id · 401 · 404 not the owner's scene or no such path · 409 too many paths · 413.

Default paths — POST /v1/scenes/<id>/paths/auto#

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/scenes/SCENE/paths
# {"scene":"SCENE","default":"p2fc0a3e33e","auto":{"id":"p2fc0a3e33e","kind":"drone","edited":false},
#  "paths":[{"id":"p2fc0a3e33e","name":"Fly-through","mode":"fly","kind":"drone","auto":true,"keys":11,…}],"canEdit":false}
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/scenes/SCENE/paths/auto -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# {"scene":"SCENE","default":true,"id":"p2fc0a3e33e","name":"Fly-through","mode":"fly","kind":"drone","auto":true,"keys":[…]}

Every scene gets a default camera path without anyone recording one: the server plans it right after the compile (and, for a scene published before, on the first read of its paths) with autopath.js and stores it as an ordinary path tagged auto: true with a kind:

  • walk — interiors and buildings: an eye-height walkthrough from the compile-time tour (tour.rs room targets, doors, gaze) refined until the baked spline never enters or brushes a wall voxel, every room of the walk grid visited, a chapter per room, 45–90 s;
  • drone — exteriors, sites, cities, captures: establishing orbit → reveal → low pass along the most open corridor → rise and look back; altitude and speed scale with the site and every point stays a clearance above the tallest voxel under it (the walk grid's height field, else the bounds), framed for low sun (the pass runs across the sun), 40–80 s;
  • orbit — products: a 360° hero orbit with a subtle push-in, 24 s.

The auto path becomes the scene's default unless the owner chose another. An owner's PUT to it makes it theirs (auto: false, from: "auto", and the list's auto.edited: true); a re-upload re-plans an unedited auto path and keeps an edited or deleted one. POST /paths/auto (owner) is "Reset to auto": it re-plans the path in place and makes it the default (422 when the scene has nothing to plan from). GET /paths/auto reads it. A share link or embed plays the default path on open with ?autoplay=path.

Guide: docs/guides/build-a-configurator.md.

Code
{
  "title": "Configure",
  "currency": "USD",
  "base": 890,
  "groups": [
    { "id": "fabric", "name": "Fabric", "default": "oak",
      "options": [
        { "id": "oak",    "name": "Oak",    "variant": "Oak" },
        { "id": "walnut", "name": "Walnut", "variant": "Walnut", "price": 120, "sku": "SOFA-WAL" } ] },
    { "id": "legs", "name": "Legs",

Later groups win a material conflict. Nothing here bills: the price total is a label.

Public, mirroring the scene's visibility (a private scene needs the owner's auth or a share token; strangers get a missing scene's 404) → { "scene", "media": [{ "material", "url", "loop", "emissive", "audio" }], "audio": [{ "pos", "url", "radius", "loop", "gain" }] }, Cache-Control: no-store. 204 No Content when the scene has neither.

PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/media#

Code
curl -sS -X PUT https://HOST/v1/scenes/SCENE/media -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"media":[{"material":3,"url":"/ingest/SCENE.media/1.mp4","emissive":1.5,"audio":true}],

# {"scene":"SCENE","media":[...],"audio":[...]}   (normalized)

Owner-only; replaces the whole table (≤ 32 KB). media: at most 4 surfaces (the renderer's media layers), each a distinct glTF material index with a same-origin video url (/ingest/<id>.media/<n>.mp4 from the upload route, or any path on this host — cross-origin URLs are refused: the frame is read back on the GPU and must not be tainted), loop (default true), emissive glow 0–8 (default 1) and audio (default false: play the video's own sound from the surface). audio: at most 16 ambient emitters, pos [x, y, z], same-origin url, radius 0.5–200 m (linear rolloff to silence), loop, gain 0–2. Errors: 400 validation (the message names the field) · 401 · 404 not the owner's scene · 409 the scene has no staging manifest (a classic GLB scene; media surfaces need a streamed scene).

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/scenes/SCENE/media/upload -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: video/mp4" --data-binary @tv-loop.mp4

Share-page tags#

A share page that names a scene (/?vpk=…, /view?glb=…, /app?…) carries, right after its <title>: <link rel="alternate" type="application/json+oembed"> (oEmbed discovery), Open Graph (og:title, og:description, og:url, og:image = the poster or the site image, with og:image:width/height) and a Twitter summary_large_image card. A private scene's page gets them only with a valid token (plus robots: noindex); without one the page is the plain app page, the same as for an unknown scene.

GET /embed#

The lazy embed card that the oEmbed html, the plug-ins and Studio's embed code frame. The same query as embed.html (vpk / glb / model / scene, look options, share, analytics=0) plus:

ParameterEffect
load=tapLoad the 3D on tap only (also the default when the browser asks to save data)
guard=0No scroll guard: the scene takes every gesture from the start (default: vertical swipes and the wheel scroll the host page until the visitor taps / clicks the scene)
fs=0No fullscreen button (default: top-right; links out to /view where the frame cannot go fullscreen, as on iPhone)
ar=0No "View in AR" control (default: shown where the device can place the scene — WebXR, or Quick Look on iOS)

It is one small HTML page: the scene's poster and title inlined, no engine. When it is 25 % visible (IntersectionObserver), or on tap, it replaces itself with embed.html (the engine), keeping the poster behind the canvas until the first frame. Headers: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp (on /embed.html too), so pages that are themselves cross-origin isolated can frame it; no X-Frame-Options. A private scene without a token gets the generic card (no title, no poster), identical to an unknown scene's.

Presence rooms#

Live-tour presence: a room is a named set of viewers who see each other's camera pose. HTTP only (SSE out, tiny POSTs in); poses are memory-only, 10 s TTL — nothing is recorded and a restart empties every room. <room> is 1–64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; treat room ids as capability URLs.

GET /v1/room/<room>/events#

text/event-stream, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. The roster arrives on connect and then on change, coalesced to ≤ ~10 frames/s:

Code
data: {"peers":[{"id":"docs-viewer-1","name":"Docs","color":"#78aaff","pose":[0,1.6,3,0,0,-1],"flags":{}}]}

2.7 (voice + presenter): open the stream as ?id=<your peer id> and it is tagged — signals addressed to that id arrive on it as named events. The first frame on a tagged or untagged stream is the config:

Code
event: config
data: {"ice":[{"urls":["stun:stun.l.google.com:19302","stun:stun1.l.google.com:19302"]}],"mesh":6}

event: signal
data: {"from":"docs-viewer-2","to":"docs-viewer-1","kind":"offer","data":{"type":"offer","sdp":"..."},"t":1760000000000}

ice is the STUN list from VERSE_STUN (comma-separated stun: URLs; none → []); mesh is the voice mesh cap (6 talkers per room). Each peer's flags object carries whichever of presenter, hand, muted, voice, ptt, host (the live tour's host) are set and the presenter's laser point [x, y, z]. The stream carries a comment line (: hb <ms>) every 5 s as a heartbeat: a client that sees 15 s of silence should reopen it. Older clients that ignore named events keep working unchanged.

  -d '{"id":"docs-viewer-1","name":"Docs","color":"#78aaff","pose":[0,1.6,3,0,0,-1]}'
# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
  • Body ≤ 2 KB: id 4–32 chars [A-Za-z0-9_-] (client-invented), name ≤ 24, color #rrggbb, pose up to 6 numbers, optional flags {presenter?, hand?, muted?, voice?, ptt?, host?, laser?: [x, y, z]} (2.7; booleans are kept only when true, anything else is dropped). Post at ~8 Hz; peers expire after 10 s of silence.
  • Errors: 400 bad id or room full (32 peers).

POST /v1/room/<room>/signal#

Relay for voice signalling and presenter events (2.7). The server forwards the body verbatim and at once to the SSE stream(s) opened with ?id=<to> — or, for to: "*", to every tagged stream in the room except the sender's — and keeps nothing. No audio ever passes through here: voice is WebRTC peer-to-peer and only the SDP / ICE text is relayed.

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/room/docs-room/signal -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from":"docs-viewer-2","to":"docs-viewer-1","kind":"offer","data":{"type":"offer","sdp":"..."}}'
# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
# X-Verse-Delivered: 1
  • Body ≤ 16 KB: from and to peer ids (4–32 chars [A-Za-z0-9_-]; to may be "*"), kind one of offer answer ice bye mute (voice), present action laser hand handover (presenter), chat, ping end (live tour, below); data any JSON.
  • Reply: 204 with X-Verse-Delivered: <n> — the number of streams the frame was written to (0 = that peer is not listening; nothing is queued).
  • Errors: 400 bad id / kind, 413 over 16 KB, 429 over 400 signals per second per room (ICE bursts are ~30 per peer), 429 too many rooms.
  • Presenter event schema (kind: "action", to: "*"), applied by followers through the same setters the UI uses: {name: "tour", detail: {playing}} · {name: "hotspot", detail: {id}} · {name: "variant", detail: {name}} · {name: "lights", detail: {query}} (a ?lights= string) · {name: "clip", detail: {encoded}} (a ?clip= string; the embed may send {planes: [[nx,ny,nz,d]…], cap} instead) · {name: "style", detail: {name}} (the restyle agent's ?style= look). present {on} announces / gives up the floor, handover {} (addressed) makes the recipient present, hand {} is a raised hand, mute {muted} mirrors the roster flag so a mute shows before the next pose post.
  • Privacy: the room id is the capability, exactly as for the roster. There is no TURN relay: two peers that both sit behind symmetric NAT never connect and the viewer says so ("no audio with …") rather than failing silently.

Tour together, live#

An agent's one tap mints a short invite link; a buyer opens it on any phone (WhatsApp / Instagram in-app browsers included) and lands in the agent's room as a guest who follows the host's camera. Three routes on top of the presence room, all memory only — an invite is {scene, room, created, expires}, no account, no name, no address; the room name is the capability and the code only shortens it. Guide: Tour together.

POST /v1/tour/invite#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/tour/invite -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scene":"ingest/5f2c…e1.vpk"}'
# {"code":"k7m2xq4","url":"https://HOST/t/k7m2xq4","room":"tour-m8w3q2vk7p","scene":"ingest/5f2c…e1.vpk",
#  "expiresAt":1760100000000,"landing":"/view?vpk=ingest%2F5f2c…e1.vpk&room=tour-m8w3q2vk7p&live=1"}
  • Body ≤ 2 KB: scene — a published scene path (ingest/<id>.vpk|.vsp|.classic.glb|.fidelity.glb; a bare <id>.vpk is normalised to ingest/), optional room (1–64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; omitted → a fresh tour-<10 random> nobody guesses).
  • Reply: code (7 chars, no 0/o/1/l/i), the absolute url (/t/<code> on the request's origin — X-Forwarded-Proto/Host are honoured), room, scene, expiresAt (ms; VERSE_TOUR_INVITE_TTL_H, default 24 h) and the landing path. Cache-Control: no-store.

  • The table holds 5 000 invites; past that the oldest tenth is dropped.

GET /v1/tour/invite/<code>#

{code, room, scene, expiresAt, landing} for a live invite, 404 for an unknown or expired code. no-store.

GET /t/<code>#

The link people open. 302 to /view?vpk=<scene>&room=<room>&live=1 (no-store); an unknown or expired code answers a small 404 HTML page ("This tour link has expired"). live=1 makes the viewer join as a guest: the Enter gate on phones, then the optional name chip, then following the host. ?room=<room>&host=1 hosts a room at once; a plain ?room= is the 2.7 viewer with the tour bar.

POST /v1/room/<room>/leave#

Code
curl -sS -X POST https://HOST/v1/room/docs-room/leave -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"id":"docs-viewer-1"}'
# HTTP/1.1 204 No Content

A page that closes says so (the viewer sends it with sendBeacon on pagehide), and the peer is dropped from the roster and rebroadcast at once instead of lingering for the 10 s TTL — the guests' "the agent left" chip must not wait on a sweep. Body ≤ 256 B, {id} (4–32 chars [A-Za-z0-9_-]); 400 bad id. Optional: a client that never sends it (the embed's own room join, older viewers) is swept after 10 s as before.

Live-tour signals and flags#

  • flags.host on the pose record marks the tour's host (the host also carries presenter: guests follow the presenter mechanics).
  • kind: "ping", to: "*", data: {pos: [x, y, z], name} — "look here": every screen draws a pulsing ring at that world point for a few seconds.
  • kind: "end", to: "*", data: {by} — the host ended the tour; guests release their cameras.
  • kind: "handover" (addressed) makes the recipient the host as well as the presenter.
  • Guests count in analytics as one act: "livetour" row per session (liveTours / live_tour_sessions in the scene report).

Signing#

GET /v1/pubkey#

The deployment's Ed25519 public key. No auth; Cache-Control: public, max-age=300.

Code
curl -sS https://HOST/v1/pubkey
# {"alg":"Ed25519","spki":"MCowBQYDK2VwAyEABHN2qIj3nOB4cvTPeA0erREzZQC1G4kpkunME6GA0B8="}

spki is base64 SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, importable as-is with crypto.subtle.importKey("spki", der, { name: "Ed25519" }, false, ["verify"]). The viewer fetches it from the host page's origin — the page embedding a scene is the trust anchor — and reports signed: true | false | "unverified". It must be identical across deploys; a changed spki means the key was not persisted and earlier scenes now read signed: false (they still load).

Floor plan to 3D home#

Turn a brochure floor plan into a furnished, walkable scene. Guide: Floor plan to 3D home. Both POSTs go through the same gates as POST /v1/ingest: the per-account/per-IP rate bucket, the key pre-check before the body, and the key and daily quota after it. A build counts as an upload of the generated GLB.

Privacy: the image goes to the Anthropic API only when the server has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set. Without it, only the built-in plan reader runs, and nothing leaves the server.

GET /v1/plan2home/status#

200 { "enabled": true, "ai": false, "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5", "styles": [{ "id": "modern-indian", "label": "Modern Indian", "blurb": "…" }, …], "defaultStyle": "modern-indian", "maxImageBytes": 25165824 }. ai is true when the AI reader is on.

POST /v1/plan2home/analyze#

  • Body: the raw image (PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF), at most 24 MB. For a PDF, the first JPEG page image is read.
  • X-Verse-Hints (optional): JSON, plain or URI-encoded. All fields are optional:
    • areaSqft or areaSqm, with areaKind set to carpet (the default), builtup or super;
    • widthM, the outside width in metres (beats the area);
    • bhk, style, city and name.
  • 200: { plan, stats, svg, ai: { used, model?, error?, tries? }, repair, validation, frame, timings }.
    • plan is the plan document. It is in metres, with x to the right and y down, and holds walls, openings and rooms (id, name, type, rects, area, center). Each opening has kind, at, width, dir, rooms, entrance and added:
      • kind is door, window or open. An open gap is an archway or a kitchen open to the living room: no leaf, and you walk through it.
      • added: true marks a door the reader put in because the drawing didn't show one.
    • repair is { added, entrance, unreachable }:
      • added is how many doors were added;
      • entrance is "moved" or "added" when the entrance was put right, else null;
      • unreachable lists the rooms that no legal door can reach (never through a bathroom, never in an outside wall). Normally it is empty.
    • validation is { ok, problems: [{ code, message, rooms? }] }: what still looks off after the readers and the repair. code is unreachable, overlapping_openings, overlapping_rooms, tiny_room (under 1.5 m² and not a toilet, store, utility or pooja), area_mismatch (the rooms' total more than 15 % off the printed total or the areaSqft / areaSqm hint; 25 % against a built-up or super area) or room_area_mismatch (a room more than 25 % off its printed area or dimensions). Check rooms lists them; the build does not refuse them (only unreachable rooms do).
    • ai.tries (only when the plan was read more than once) lists each reading: { model, problems? | error? }. A reading that fails validation is read again by a stronger model (see VERSE_PLAN_ESCALATE), and the reading with the fewest problems wins.
    • frame is { imageW, imageH, pxPerM, origin, deskew? }: image pixel = (plan metres + origin) × pxPerM, before the deskew rotation (radians, about the image centre) is undone. Use it to draw the plan over the upload.
    • stats gives the rooms by type, the carpet area and the BHK.
    • svg is the plan drawn for display.
    • ai.error is set when the AI reader was on but failed. In that case the built-in reader's plan is returned.
  • Errors:
    • 413: over the size limit.
    • 415: not a PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF.
    • 422: no plan could be read, or the image is not a floor plan (a photo of a room, a render). The error field says why, in words meant for the user.
    • 503: two plans are already being read; retry after Retry-After.

POST /v1/plan2home/build#

  • Body (JSON, ≤ 1 MB): { "plan": <plan from analyze, edited>, "style": "modern-indian" | "scandinavian" | "luxury" | "minimal", "name": "Sunrise 2BHK" }.
  • What it does: generates the furnished GLB. Before publishing, it walks the home from the entrance on a 10 cm grid.
  • 202: { job, id, statusUrl, experienceUrl, checks, stats }.
    • Follow statusUrl (GET /v1/ingest/<job>) exactly as for an upload.
    • When the job is done, <id>.stage.json holds the spawn at the living-room entrance, with a walk view. ingest/exp-<hex>.verse.json holds one hotspot per room and a guided tour, and it is the scene's default experience when an account owns the scene.
    • experienceUrl opens the scene with the room hotspots.
  • Errors:
    • 400: the plan is malformed.
    • 422 { "code": "unreachable_rooms", "unreachable": [{ "id", "name" }] }: a room cannot be reached from the entrance (usually a missing door). Nothing is published. The plan is built exactly as sent, so the build adds no doors. Add one in the plan (Check rooms: Edit doors), or send the plan that analyze returned, which is already repaired.
    • 503 server_busy: the compile queue is full.

Assistant#

The endpoint behind Ask Verse, the site assistant. Guide: Ask Verse. It has no server-side side effects and no access to accounts, tokens, scenes or files: it returns text plus UI actions from a fixed whitelist, which the page validates again and runs itself.

POST /v1/assist#

  • Body (JSON, ≤ 48 KB): { "messages": [{ "role": "user" | "assistant", "content": "…" }], "context": { "surface": "landing" | "app" | "studio" | "docs", "path": "/app", "sceneLoaded": true } }. The first and last message must be from the user. At most 20 messages, 1,000 characters in the newest one.
  • Response: 200 text/event-stream. Each data: line is one JSON event:
Code
data: {"type":"text","delta":"Opening the upload panel."}
data: {"type":"action","action":{"type":"open_upload"}}
data: {"type":"done","mode":"ai"}

text events are appended in order; action events arrive after the text; done carries the mode that answered (ai or basic); an error event means the reply was cut short and no action should run.

  • Actions (the whole list): navigate {path} (only /, /app, /studio, /docs/ and product-page sections), open_upload, load_demo {name}, start_tour {surface, chapter?}, set_view {mode} (walk, orbit, tour, stop_tour, minimap, measure), export_video, open_review, share_link, open_docs {page, section?} (public docs pages only), show_limits {limits}. At most 3 per reply.
  • Errors carry { "error": "…", "message": "…" }, where message is written for the visitor: 400 (malformed or too long), 403 (cross-site request), 429 (per-IP bucket), 503 (daily cap reached, busy, or unavailable).
Code
curl -N -X POST "$VERSE/v1/assist" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"how big can my file be?"}],"context":{"surface":"landing"}}'

{ "mode": "ai" } when the server has ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, { "mode": "basic" } otherwise (a deterministic local responder: curated intents plus a search over the public docs headings).

Compile fleet: /v1/work/*#

Pull API for external compile workers (tools/verse-worker). Every route requires Authorization: Bearer $VERSE_WORKER_TOKEN; while the variable is unset the routes answer 404, a wrong token 401. Jobs unclaimed for 10 s, or claimed but silent for 20 min, fall back to the origin's local compiler, so zero workers is exactly the single-box behaviour.

RouteWhat
GET /v1/work/claimClaim the oldest unclaimed job. 204 = nothing to do; 200 = { "id", "images": bool, "source": "/v1/work/<id>/source" }. X-Verse-Worker: <name> is credited as workedBy.
GET /v1/work/<id>/sourceThe uploaded GLB bytes.
GET /v1/work/<id>/imagesThe KTX2 RGBA sidecar for --images, or 404.
POST /v1/work/<id>/stage{ "stage": "<a-z->" } progress shown live to the uploader; 204. "worker-failed" hands the job back to the origin immediately.
POST /v1/work/<id>/resultThe finished .vpk bytes; stats in X-Verse-Tris / X-Verse-Clusters. 204; 410 = the job already finished elsewhere.

The origin signs delivered files itself; workers never hold the key. Splat jobs are never offered to the fleet.

Fleet bake. A worker that sends X-Verse-Caps: bake on its claims is counted for "Bake for me" splits (seen in the last 15 s) and is offered bake parts before compile jobs; workers without the header never see them. A bake is split into 1 + (such workers), at most 8, parts (VERSE_BAKE_PARTS on the origin forces a count); part 0 runs on the origin. A bake-part claim answers:

Code
{ "id": "villa-9f3a01b2c4d5~bake2", "kind": "bake-part", "quality": "final",
  "part": 2, "parts": 3, "deadlineS": 1041, "source": "/v1/work/villa-9f3a01b2c4d5~bake2/source" }

The worker downloads source (the prepared GLB the origin is baking), runs verse-compile --bake <quality> in.glb --part <part>/<parts> --deadline-s <deadlineS> -o part.vbp, heartbeats POST …/stage ({"stage":"baking"}), and posts the part file to POST …/result (204; 410/404 = the bake already finished without it). The origin drops it into its coordinator's part directory; a part with a different plan fingerprint is ignored, and a part that does not arrive in time is baked on the origin — a slow or vanished worker costs time, never the bake. deadlineS is what is left of the origin's own deadline.
